items.text: InBook1,youlearned aboutstructuralisomerism anditsdivisionintochainisomerism andposition isomerism.You then considered a different type of isomerism called'geometric isomerism',including the termsE-Z and cis-trans isomerism-thisisonetypeofstereoisomerism.

items.label: text
items.text: This chapterlooks at a second type of stereoisomerism-opticalisomerism.Before we introduce this,it is useful to consider all the types of isomerism thatyou need to befamiliarwith, in the form of a family tree.

items.label: text
items.text: Structural isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but with different structural formulae.

items.label: text
items.text: Functional group isomers differ because they have different functional groups (e.g. aldehydes and ketones, alcohols and ethers).

items.label: text
items.text: Chain isomers differ because they have different patterns of branching in their carbon chains.

items.label: text
items.text: Positional isomers differ because the same functional group is attached to different carbon atoms in the chain.

items.label: text
items.text: Geometricisomers differbecause their atoms orgroups are attached at different positions on opposite sides of a C=C double bond.

items.label: text
items.text: Howdoesopticalisomerismfitintothisfamilytree?Opticalisomersarenon-superimposablemirror images of each otherbut are otherwise the same.This needs careful explanation!
